name: The First-Touch Unboxing
why_it_works: Unboxing lets the viewer borrow the feeling of receiving a gift. Slowing down each layer (ribbon, tissue, note) builds anticipation, and seeing the product touch skin or fabric at the end makes it feel already theirs.

hook.pattern: Open on the sealed package with a sensory sound and a promise about what is inside.
examples: The box is half the gift. Look inside.
This is what {{brand}} sends when you order.
Unboxing our {{product}} like it's your first time.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 overhead shot of a closed {{brand}} box with {{packaging_detail}} on a linen tablecloth, soft morning window light, minimal props
Hands slowly lifting the lid off the {{brand}} box and parting tissue paper, soft window light, overhead locked-off vertical 9:16
Close-up of a small printed card reading the brand note tucked into tissue, warm light, shallow depth of field, vertical 9:16

beats.purpose: the first touch: product in use

visual.prompt: The {{product}} lifted from the box and used for the first time, close-up on hands and texture, soft natural light, slow motion, vertical 9:16

craft.notes: Each layer of packaging is a mini-reveal; give each its own beat and its own sound (crinkle, snap, slide). The product appears only in the final motion beat, in use, never sitting still on a white background.

do_not: Rush the open in one cut; the delay is the point
Show packaging that customers do not actually receive
Make skin, health or body claims in the note or voiceover
compliance: Supplements: no claims to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease; include the standard FDA disclaimer when any benefit is stated
Supplements: no before/after body images or weight-loss numbers
Skincare: cosmetic claims only (looks, feels); no medical claims like 'heals' or 'treats acne' unless the product is approved for it
